4.grammar: A relational adjective formed with the -iyy suffix ('belonging to / characterized by'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it qualifies ('an Arabic …').

5.meaning: And We distributed, varied, and laid out in diverse forms — to turn a matter over and present it in many ways, repeating and varying it so it is fully made clear.
5.grammar: An intensive past-tense verb (the doubled middle root letter gives the sense of doing thoroughly or repeatedly) prefixed with 'and'. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we did …').
5.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn, divert, vary; hence to set forth in changing, diverse forms

6.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

7.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

8.meaning: The threat, the menacing warning — a forewarning of punishment or dire consequence held out as a deterrent.
8.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the threat'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case ending, used after a preposition or to follow a preceding noun as something it is linked to ('… OF …').
8.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise; in this form specifically a promise of harm, i.e. a threat

9.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

9.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
9.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

10.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
10.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
10.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

11.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
11.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

12.meaning: It brings about, produces, or causes to newly arise — to originate something fresh that did not exist before.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb of the causative pattern ('to make something come about'). The yu- prefix indicates a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it does …'). The final -u (ḍamma) marks the indicative mood, the plain factual form of the verb.
12.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — newness; to come about, to originate, to bring something new into being

13.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

14.meaning: A mention, a remembrance, a reminder; calling something to mind or speaking of it, and by extension a piece of admonition or scripture.
14.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The -an ending (tanwin) is the indefinite accusative, typically marking a direct object ('a remembrance') or a specification.
14.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

1.meaning: 'So He is exalted high above (it)' or 'then He is far transcendent.' Built on a verb meaning to be lofty/elevated, this form expresses that someone is utterly high and above something — used of Allah being far beyond any deficiency or false association. The opening fa- links it to what precedes as a consequence.
1.grammar: A 'he' verb expressing height and transcendence. The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence. The verb pattern intensifies the sense of being elevated and removed far above something lower.
1.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'The king' — the sovereign ruler who holds dominion and authority over a realm and its people.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the king'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate.
3.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule, hold dominion

4.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
4.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: 'Do not be hasty / hurry / rush' — a verb about seeking something too quickly, acting before the proper time, or being impatient. It is the form used after a prohibition word ('do not…').
6.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The verb is present tense, and the bare, vowel-less final consonant (the jussive form) is the shape used after a prohibitive 'do not', giving a command not to do something ('do not hurry').
6.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — to hasten, hurry, be impatient

7.meaning: With/by the Qur'an — al-Qur'ān, literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading,' the revealed Scripture meant to be recited aloud.
7.grammar: A definite verbal noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive case ending, the case required after a preposition.
7.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — to read, to recite, to gather words in recitation

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
8.root: — (preposition)

9.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
9.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
9.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: It is decreed, decided, carried out, or brought to completion — to settle a matter fully and conclusively, finishing it off.
11.grammar: A present-tense passive verb ('it is being decreed/completed'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, and the passive vowelling shows the action is done to it rather than by it. The final long -ā belongs to this weak-ending verb; in the present such a verb's last vowel is not separately pronounced for case.
11.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, decide, carry out, bring to a conclusive end

12.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
12.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

13.meaning: Its revelation, its inspiration — waḥy is the act and content of divine disclosure, words and meaning conveyed swiftly and secretly from Allah to a chosen recipient.
13.grammar: A verbal noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u (ḍamma) before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the subject of a sentence. The suffix -hu means 'his/its', showing possession.
13.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to disclose swiftly and secretly; divine inspiration, revelation

14.meaning: And say — a command to one person to utter or speak words. The plain, central act of speaking aloud.
14.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male, 'say!' from a hollow verb (middle root letter 'w' drops out in the command). The vowel-less ending is the standard singular masculine imperative. Prefixed wa- 'and' joins it to a preceding clause.
14.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

15.meaning: Lord and Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and has full authority over a thing; a term combining ownership, care, and lordship that goes beyond any single English word.
15.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of / belonging to' relationship, or follows a preposition or oath particle. 'Rabb' denotes a master who owns, sustains, and nurtures what is under his charge.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery and ownership

16.meaning: Increase me, give me more, add to what I have — a request to be granted a greater measure of something.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person ('increase!'), with no case vowel since commands rest on the bare verb form. The attached -nī means 'me,' the one receiving the action (its 'n' is a connector that protects the verb before the 'me').
16.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, add, grow, give more

17.meaning: Knowledge — that which is known; firm, certain awareness and understanding.
17.grammar: An abstract noun, 'knowledge.' The final -an is the accusative with indefinite 'nunation,' commonly marking the noun as a direct object, or as a specification ('in respect of knowledge').

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We enjoined, charged, or made a binding covenant — to lay down a solemn commitment or entrust a pledge to someone.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we did …'). The long final -ā here is the spelling of that 'we' ending.
2.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, solemn charge or commitment

3.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
3.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

4.meaning: 'Adam' — the proper name of the first human being and first prophet.
4.grammar: A proper name that is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — it takes a restricted set of endings. Its final -a here does double duty: it marks the accusative case (e.g., as a direct object) and, because the name is a diptote, it stands in place of the usual nominative -u while also blocking the tanwīn (-n) that fully inflected nouns would take.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
6.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'he forgot, neglected, or let slip from memory', joined to a connector 'but/so/then'. It conveys losing hold of something in the mind, or failing to keep it in view.
7.grammar: Past-tense verb with prefixed 'fa-' ('so/then', marking sequence or consequence). It is third-person masculine singular ('he …'). The root's final weak letter surfaces as the '-iya' sound at the end. The sense is forgetting or neglecting.
7.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, leave behind

8.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
8.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

9.meaning: We found, came upon, or discovered — to encounter something or to find it to be a certain way.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix indicates a first-person plural subject ('we do …'). The vowel-less final consonant marks the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'not' or 'if'.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, discover, perceive to be

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: Firm resolve, steadfast determination, settled purpose — a binding resolution of the will to see something through.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun. The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness; such an ending often signals the object of a verb ('to find … resolve').
11.root: ع-ز-م (ʿ-z-m) — to resolve firmly, to be determined, settled purpose of will

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'We said' — the act of speaking or uttering, completed in the past, with 'we' as the speakers (a plural, or the royal/majestic 'We').
2.grammar: A past-tense verb 'to say' with the suffix '-nā' marking the doer as 'we' (first-person plural). This is a hollow verb (its middle root letter is a weak 'w'), which contracts before the suffix to leave 'qul-' before the ending.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

3.meaning: 'To the angels' — the preposition 'to / for' joined to the definite plural 'the angels', the beings created of light who serve and obey.
3.grammar: A preposition + the definite article + a noun. The prefix li- ('to / for') places the noun in the genitive state, shown by the final -i. The l- is the definite article 'the'. The -at- is a feminine/collective ending on the plural 'angels'. So the genitive -i here is triggered by the preposition 'to / for'.

4.meaning: 'Prostrate! / bow down!' — a command to a group to lower themselves to the ground in prostration, the posture of deepest humility and submission.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb meaning 'prostrate / bow down'. It begins with a helping vowel (the initial 'u-') to ease pronunciation; the ending '-ū' (written with a silent trailing alif) directs the command to a plural 'you all'.

5.meaning: 'To Adam' — the preposition 'to / for' joined to the proper name Adam, the first human being, indicating direction or recipient.
5.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to, for') attached to the proper name 'Ādam'. After this preposition the name takes a final -a; as a non-fully-inflecting (diptote) proper noun, it shows -a in the genitive position rather than the usual -i.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and so they prostrated / fell down in prostration' — lowering oneself to the ground in submission and worship.

parts.en: they (masculine plural); the alif is a silent spelling

6.grammar: A past-tense verb opened by the connector fa- ('so/then', marking a result or sequence). The stem is sajad-, and the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural): fa-sajad-ū. The alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
6.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in submission

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

8.meaning: Iblīs, the proper name of the rebellious creature (from among the jinn) who refused the divine command to prostrate to Adam. The name is associated with despair and being cut off from divine mercy.
8.grammar: A proper noun. As a non-Arabic (foreign) name it behaves as a diptote, so its ending appears as -a (here the accusative) rather than the usual -i in genitive contexts. The -a typically marks a word as the object of a verb or governed by certain particles.

9.meaning: He refused, declined, or held back from doing something — a willful, persistent refusal to comply.

parts.en: final root letter (ي), written as alif maqṣūra

9.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he refused'). This is a defective (final-weak) verb whose third root letter is y; in the past tense that final radical surfaces as a long -ā written with alif maqṣūra (ى). The 'he' (3rd-person masculine singular) is carried by a zero suffix, not by any added letter, and the action is presented as completed.
9.root: أ-ب-ي (ʾ-b-y) — to refuse, decline

1.meaning: 'So/then We said'. It combines a connector with the past-tense verb 'to say' done by 'we'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed fa- ('so/then', showing sequence). The suffix -nā is the attached pronoun 'we', marking the subject of a completed act of speaking.

2.meaning: A vocative call meaning 'O Adam!' — the address-particle yā placed before the proper name Adam to summon or call out to him directly.
2.grammar: yā is the particle of calling/address ('O…'). The name after it stands in the vocative; the final -u is the typical ending for a single, definite name being called directly, marking it as the one summoned.

3.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
3.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'adversary' — one who shows hostility or opposition. The single Arabic form can refer to one enemy or collectively to enemies.
5.grammar: A noun carrying the -un ending: nominative case (typically the subject, or the completing word after 'to be') combined with tanwīn, the indefinite '-n' that marks it as 'an enemy' rather than 'the enemy'.
5.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — hostility, enmity, transgressing a limit

6.meaning: 'To you / for you' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the singular addressee 'you' (masculine). It marks direction, benefit, or possession ('belonging to you').
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with an attached pronoun. The suffix -ka means 'you' (masculine singular). The fixed -a vowel on -ka is simply how this object pronoun is voweled; the whole unit means 'to/for you.' (The doubled 'l' reflects assimilation to a preceding word.)

7.meaning: A linked phrase: 'and for/to your spouse' — combining 'and', the preposition 'for/to', the noun 'spouse/mate', and 'your'. Zawj denotes a partner of a pair (husband or wife).
7.grammar: wa- joins this to what precedes; the preposition li- ('for/to') forces the following noun into the genitive, shown by the -i on zawj-. The attached -ka means 'your', addressing one male.
7.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pairing, mating, joining as a couple

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

9.meaning: A strongly emphasized warning-verb: 'he will most certainly drive you both out / expel you two'. From the sense of causing someone to go out or be expelled.
9.grammar: The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular ('he') in a causative pattern ('make go out / expel'). The doubled -nna is the heavy emphatic ending, giving the force 'will surely/certainly'. The suffix -kumā is the object 'you two' (dual).
9.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, exiting, expulsion

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
11.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
11.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

12.meaning: 'so that you would toil/suffer hardship' — to be wretched, to labor in misery, to be deprived of ease.
12.grammar: fa- signals consequence ('so/then'). The ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular ('you'). The verb ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is a weak vowel; in this present-tense form it is left in its base (unmarked) mood.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
2.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
2.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

3.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
3.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

4.meaning: 'you go hungry / will be hungry' — to feel hunger, to lack food.
4.grammar: The ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular ('you') in the present tense. The final -a here is the ending used when the verb is governed into the subjunctive (e.g. after a particle such as 'that' / 'so that').

5.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
5.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
5.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: 'you are/become naked, uncovered, bare' — to be without clothing.
7.grammar: The ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular ('you') in the present tense. The verb ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak; the form sits in its base (unmarked) mood.
7.root: ع-ر-ي (ʿ-r-y) — nakedness, being bare or uncovered

1.meaning: 'and that you…' — the connector 'and' joined to the emphatic particle anna ('that, indeed') with 'you' attached. Anna affirms a fact and introduces a noun-clause ('the fact that you…').
1.grammar: wa- joins this to a previous statement. anna is an emphatic/affirming particle ('that indeed…') that introduces and governs a following clause, placing its subject in the accusative — here the attached -ka ('you', one male) is that subject.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: 'you are/become thirsty, suffer thirst' — to feel thirst, to need to drink.
3.grammar: The ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular ('you') in the present tense. The final -u is the plain indicative ending, the form used for a simple present/future statement ('you are/will be thirsty').

4.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
4.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: 'you are exposed to the scorching sun / suffer the sun's heat' — to be out under the blazing midday sun without shade.

parts.en: be exposed to the sun's heat

6.grammar: The ta- prefix marks second-person masculine singular ('you') in the present tense. The verb ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak; the form rests in its base (unmarked) mood.
6.root: ض-ح-و (ḍ-ḥ-w) — daylight/forenoon, being out in the open sun

1.meaning: 'Then he whispered / made insidious suggestions.' Beginning with 'then,' it uses a verb describing low, repeated, hidden prompting — the subtle inner whisper of an evil suggestion or temptation.
1.grammar: The connective fa ('then / so,' marking sequence) plus a third-person masculine singular past-tense verb ('he whispered'). The verb is a reduplicated four-letter form whose doubled sound mimics a faint, repeated whispering. The bare past form indicates a completed act by 'he.'

2.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

3.meaning: Shayṭān / Satan — a rebellious, malevolent being who incites to evil; the term denotes one that is remote from goodness and given to misleading. With 'al-', it points to the well-known devil.
3.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'sh', doubling it). 'shayṭān' is a noun for a devil or inciter of evil. The final -u is nominative, the form a word takes as the subject or doer of an action.

4.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
4.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

5.meaning: A vocative call meaning 'O Adam!' — the address-particle yā placed before the proper name Adam to summon or call out to him directly.
5.grammar: yā is the particle of calling/address ('O…'). The name after it stands in the vocative; the final -u is the typical ending for a single, definite name being called directly, marking it as the one summoned.

6.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
6.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

7.meaning: 'shall I point/guide you to it?, I direct you' — to show someone the way to something, to indicate or lead toward it.
7.grammar: The a- prefix marks first-person singular ('I') in the present tense. The base ending is the plain indicative -u (a simple 'I show/direct'). The attached -ka is the object 'you' (one male) — the one being shown the way.
7.root: د-ل-ل (d-l-l) — pointing out, indicating, guiding to something

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'tree' — a tree or woody plant; also used collectively for trees/vegetation.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -ti (the feminine 'closed tāʾ' ending pronounced -t- here) carries the -i genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
9.root: ش-ج-ر (sh-j-r) — trees, growth of woody plants

10.meaning: Endlessness, perpetual abiding, everlastingness — remaining forever without ceasing.
10.grammar: A singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF endlessness') or follows a preposition ('of / for everlasting life').

11.meaning: 'and a dominion/kingdom/sovereignty' — possession of royal authority and a realm; kingship and ownership of a domain.
11.grammar: wa- joins this to what precedes. The noun is indefinite ('a kingdom'); the final -in (written with two short marks, 'tanwīn') is the indefinite genitive ending, the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun.
11.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, kingship, sovereignty

12.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
12.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

13.meaning: 'it wears out, decays, comes to an end' — to grow old and worn, to fade and perish over time.
13.grammar: The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('it/he') in the present tense. The verb ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak; the form sits in its base (unmarked) mood, expressing an ongoing/future 'wears out'.
13.root: ب-ل-ي (b-l-y) — wearing out, decaying, growing old and worn

1.meaning: 'so they two ate' — the consequence-marker 'so/then' joined to the past-tense verb 'to eat', done by two people.
1.grammar: fa- signals sequence/consequence ('so then'). akala is the past-tense verb 'ate'; the attached long -ā (the dual ending on a past verb) marks the doers as two ('they both').

2.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
2.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

3.meaning: 'so it appeared / became visible' — the marker 'so/then' joined to the past-tense verb 'to become apparent', with a feminine doer.
3.grammar: fa- signals sequence/consequence ('so then'). bada(t) is the past-tense verb 'became apparent'; the silent -t ending marks the doer as feminine singular ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine noun as subject.
3.root: ب-د-و (b-d-w) — appearing, becoming visible, emerging into view

4.meaning: 'To them both / for the two of them' — a preposition meaning 'to / for' joined to a pronoun referring to exactly two people, indicating something directed toward or belonging to that pair.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for,' often marking a recipient, beneficiary, or possessor) with its vowel shifting to 'a' before a pronoun, joined to the dual pronoun -humā ('the two of them'). The -humā ending specifically denotes two persons.

5.meaning: 'the private/shameful parts of the two of them' — the bodily nakedness one naturally seeks to conceal; literally that which it grieves a person to have exposed, belonging to two people.
5.grammar: A noun (from the sense of what causes shame/grief if uncovered) carrying a possessive suffix. The final -u (damma) on the feminine 'closed tāʾ' is the nominative ending, the form a noun takes as the subject/doer. The attached -humā means 'of the two of them' (dual possessor).
5.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — evil, that which is shameful or grievous; what one is ashamed to expose

6.meaning: And the two of them set about / began — to start or take up doing something. This verb introduces an action that the two subjects then commence.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the dual subject ending -ā ('the two of them did'). It belongs to the class of 'verbs of beginning,' which are followed by another verb describing what was started. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
6.root: ط-ف-ق (ṭ-f-q) — to begin, to set about doing something

7.meaning: The two of them stitch/lay over — to layer or fasten one thing over another, as in covering a surface by piling or sewing pieces together. The form has a dual subject acting in the present/ongoing sense.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -āni ending marks a dual ('the two of them are doing'); the retained final -ni shows the verb is in its indicative (plain statement) mood rather than being cut off by a governing particle.
7.root: خ-ص-ف (kh-ṣ-f) — to stitch or patch together, lay one layer over another

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon the two of them,' 'on both of them,' 'against them two.' It places a duty, blame, or claim on exactly two parties.
8.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- before an attached pronoun, often conveying obligation or something weighing on someone. The suffix -himā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them'; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
9.root: — (preposition)

10.meaning: Leaves / foliage — the leaf-growth of a tree or plant, especially the broad leaves used as covering. A collective noun for leaves taken together.
10.grammar: A noun in the genitive case, shown by the final -i ending. The genitive typically links the word to a following noun ('the leaves OF …') or follows a preposition. (The doubled w- at the start reflects assimilation with a preceding word in connected recitation.)
10.root: و-ر-ق (w-r-q) — foliage, leaves; also paper/leaf as a sheet

11.meaning: 'the Garden' — a lush, enclosed garden of trees; the term used for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of bliss.
11.grammar: al- is 'the', making the noun definite. The feminine 'closed tāʾ' ending here carries the -i genitive case, the form used after a preposition or linking to a preceding noun ('… of the Garden').
11.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; a garden whose trees veil the ground

12.meaning: 'and he disobeyed / went against (a command)' — to defy and refuse to comply with an order.
12.grammar: wa- joins this to what precedes. ʿaṣā is a past-tense verb done by a third-person masculine singular ('he'); it ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak, the normal shape of such a past-tense 'he did' verb.
12.root: ع-ص-ي (ʿ-ṣ-y) — disobedience, rebellion against a command

13.meaning: The proper name 'Adam' — the first human being and prophet in the Islamic tradition.
13.grammar: A proper name carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer of its clause. As a foreign/diptote name it takes no tanwīn (no indefinite '-n').

14.meaning: The noun 'Lord' joined to a 'his' pronoun — 'his Lord'. Rabb conveys the Master and Sustainer who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; far richer than 'lord' alone.
14.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hu ('his'). The -a ending is accusative, the case used when the noun is an object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case; -hu means it belongs to 'him'.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

15.meaning: 'so he erred / went astray / fell into error' — to deviate from the right course, to lose one's way and slip into wrongdoing or frustrated hopes.
15.grammar: fa- signals consequence ('so then'). ghawā is a past-tense verb done by a third-person masculine singular ('he'); it ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak, the usual form of such a past 'he did' verb.
15.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — going astray, error, deviation from right guidance

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'he chose/selected him' — to pick out and favor someone, drawing them near for a special purpose. From the sense of gathering and singling out the best.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'choose for oneself / single out' pattern, done by a third-person masculine singular ('he'); the long -ā before the suffix is the weak final letter of such a verb. The attached -hu is the object 'him' (the one chosen).
2.root: ج-ب-ي (j-b-y) — gathering, collecting; selecting and singling out

3.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer. 'Rabb' denotes the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings a thing to its completion; the attached pronoun makes it 'his.'
3.grammar: A noun followed by a possessive pronoun. The -u on 'rabb' is the nominative ending, the case used for the subject/doer of a sentence ('the one who does'). The attached -hu means 'his.'
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'then he turned' — built on a root for repentance and turning back. Of a servant it means turning to Allah in repentance; of Allah it means turning toward a servant with forgiveness and mercy.
4.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', marking a consequence or next step) joined to a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he turned'). The action is complete. The direction of the 'turning' (a servant repenting, or Allah forgiving) is shown by the preposition that follows it.

5.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
5.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

6.meaning: 'and he guided / showed the right way' — to direct someone to the correct path and lead them rightly.
6.grammar: wa- joins this to what precedes. hadā is a past-tense verb done by a third-person masculine singular ('he'); it ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak, the standard form of such a past 'he did' verb.
6.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right path, leading rightly

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'go down, both of you / descend, you two' — a command to two people to come down or descend from a higher place.
2.grammar: A direct command (imperative). It begins with a helping vowel (the initial alif) needed to pronounce the cluster, and the attached -ā ending directs the order at two people ('both of you go down').
2.root: ه-ب-ط (h-b-ṭ) — descending, going down to a lower place

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
3.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

4.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
5.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.
5.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, some

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to some' or 'for another part'. It marks the recipient or counterpart in a reciprocal pairing, the 'other side' that 'some of you' relate to.
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') attached to the noun 'a part/some'. The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'): the genitive case is required after the preposition, and the tanwīn marks the noun as indefinite ('a part', not 'the part').
6.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, some

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'adversary' — one who shows hostility or opposition. The single Arabic form can refer to one enemy or collectively to enemies.
7.grammar: A noun carrying the -un ending: nominative case (typically the subject, or the completing word after 'to be') combined with tanwīn, the indefinite '-n' that marks it as 'an enemy' rather than 'the enemy'.
7.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — hostility, enmity, transgressing a limit

8.meaning: A compound conditional expression meaning 'then if ever' or 'so whenever'. It combines 'then/so' with a conditional 'if' to introduce a case that may arise, usually paired with a following emphasis on the verb.
8.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so') joined to immā, itself the conditional particle 'in' ('if') merged with an emphasising mā. It sets up a condition — 'if it should happen that…' — and characteristically leads to a verb reinforced with a strong 'certainly' ending.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'it shall surely come to you' or 'it will certainly reach you (plural)'. It expresses an action of coming/arriving directed at a group, stamped with heavy emphasis that it definitely will occur.
9.grammar: A present/future verb 'comes' (third-person masculine singular, 'he/it'), reinforced by the heavy emphatic ending -anna ('shall surely'), and followed by the object pronoun -kum ('you all'). Before this heavy emphatic ending the verb keeps its final -ya vowel (yatiya-). The -anna is the strong-affirmation ending that pairs with a preceding conditional, stressing the action will certainly happen.
9.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving, bringing

10.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'from Me'. It marks a source or origin as the speaker's own self.
10.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached first-person pronoun 'me'. An extra n is doubled with the pronoun's n so the word ends -nnī, the standard way 'from' joins to 'me'. The whole marks the speaker as the point of origin: 'from Me'.

11.meaning: 'guidance' — right direction, the showing of the true path; the gift of being led correctly. A core Qur'anic term for divinely given direction toward truth.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun ('guidance') whose third root letter is weak, written as the final alif maqsūra (not a separable suffix). The -an ending it carries is the 'tanwīn' nunation marking the accusative — the form a noun takes as an object or in similar non-subject roles.
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right path, leading rightly

12.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then whoever'. It joins a clause to what precedes ('so', 'then') and introduces a conditional or general statement about any person who does something ('whoever, anyone who').
12.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so/then', linking this to a prior statement. man is a conditional/relative word for persons ('whoever'); its base form is man, and the final vowel here is read -i simply to ease pronunciation before a following consonant cluster, not a case ending.

13.meaning: Means 'he followed / pursued' — to go after something and adopt it, walking in its path or seeking it out, whether following a person, a way, or an aim.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with a built-in doer 'he' (a single male): 'he followed.' It is built on the reflexive ift'aʿala pattern (which inserts a -t- after the first root letter); this pattern adds the sense of actively pursuing or making something one's own. Here the first root letter ت merges with that inserted -t-, producing the doubled ت heard at the start (it-ta-) — so the doubling is at the front from this merging, not in the middle root letter. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending.
13.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

14.meaning: 'My guidance' — guidance, right direction, or the showing of the correct path, combined with the possessive 'my.' The base noun denotes divinely-given direction that leads one rightly.
14.grammar: A noun, 'guidance' (hudā), whose own final letter is the long vowel alif maqsura. The first-person possessive 'my' attaches to that final vowel and surfaces as '-ya' (rather than the usual '-ī'), so the whole reads 'my guidance.' The possessor 'my' is carried by this '-ya', not by a separate stem letter.
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the right way

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

16.meaning: He goes astray / strays / errs / is lost — to wander from the right path, lose one's way, or fall into error. The doubled final consonant belongs to the root.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person-masculine-singular subject ('he'). The two identical final root letters are merged (a doubled consonant), and the -u vowel on it marks the indicative mood, a plain statement ('he strays').
16.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: 'he toils / suffers hardship, becomes wretched' — to labor in misery, to fall into distress and lose ease and well-being.
18.grammar: The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he') in the present tense. The verb ends in a long -ā because its final root letter is weak; the form rests in its base (unmarked) mood, expressing an ongoing/future 'toils / will suffer'.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'he turned away' or 'he averted himself' — deliberately turning aside from something, shunning or disregarding it.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final '-a' marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular). This Form IV verb conveys deliberately turning one's side away from something — to shun, avoid, or disregard it.
2.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — side; (Form IV) to turn away from

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: 'My remembrance / My reminder' — the act of calling to mind, mentioning, and being mindful, tied to a possessor: remembrance OF me, or my mention of something.
4.grammar: A verbal noun with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending fixes the word's case, so it reads simply 'my remembrance / my reminder'.
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, calling to mind

5.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
5.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: A way of living, a livelihood; the means and conditions by which one sustains life, and the totality of one's daily existence and the resources that support it.
7.grammar: A noun built on a place/manner pattern from the verb 'to live'. The final -an with tanwīn is the indefinite accusative: it marks the word as 'a living' functioning as an object or predicate, and the doubled-n sound signals that it is indefinite (without 'the'). The feminine ta-marbuta is sounded as -t- before this ending.

8.meaning: Cramped, narrow, tight and distressing; a life or condition that is constricted, hard, and full of hardship, the opposite of ease and spaciousness.
8.grammar: A descriptive noun used adjectivally. The final -an with tanwīn is the indefinite accusative ending, typically marking it as an object or as a quality describing an indefinite accusative noun.
8.root: ض-ن-ك (ḍ-n-k) — narrowness, tightness, straitened hardship

9.meaning: And We gather/herd him together — to drive and assemble someone, collecting people into one place as a crowd is mustered.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The na- prefix means 'we' (the speaker plus others), and the verb's plain ending marks it as ongoing or future action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him'.
9.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather, herd, assemble

10.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
10.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

11.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
11.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

12.meaning: Lacking sight; one who cannot see. The word denotes a person or thing characterized by blindness, and is frequently used in a figurative sense for spiritual or moral blindness — an inability to perceive truth or guidance.
12.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive 'afʿal' pattern used for bodily traits, masculine singular. It denotes a permanent characteristic ('blind') rather than a passing state. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings.

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
2.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
3.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

4.meaning: You gathered/raised me up — to assemble and bring someone forth, said of being mustered or resurrected by the one addressed.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ta ending means the subject is 'you' (one male). The attached -nī is the object pronoun 'me', with its protective -n- linking the verb to the pronoun.

5.meaning: Lacking sight; one who cannot see. The word denotes a person or thing characterized by blindness, and is frequently used in a figurative sense for spiritual or moral blindness — an inability to perceive truth or guidance.
5.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive 'afʿal' pattern used for bodily traits, masculine singular. It denotes a permanent characteristic ('blind') rather than a passing state. Its final long 'ā' is fixed and does not change for the usual case-endings.
5.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight

6.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
6.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
7.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

8.meaning: All-Seeing — one who sees fully and perfectly. An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) expressing sight as a permanent, comprehensive attribute that misses nothing.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate after certain particles — and the -n shows it is indefinite ('a seer / seeing').
8.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, perception

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
2.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
2.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

3.meaning: She/it came to you — the arrival of something (often a feminine noun such as a sign, message, or warning) reaching the one addressed.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -t ending marks the subject as feminine singular ('she/it'). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male), so the whole is 'it came to you'.

4.meaning: Our signs / verses — 'āyāt' are tokens, proofs, and miraculous indications that point to a deeper truth, and also the verses of revelation; with 'Our' it refers to such signs ascribed to Allah.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs, verses') with the attached possessive 'our' = -nā. The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the subject/naming case, the form a noun takes as the doer or topic of a sentence ('Our signs [are/do...]').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token, miraculous indication

5.meaning: So you forgot it/her — to let something slip from memory and neglect it, with the connecting word 'so/then' linking it to what precedes.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb with a prefixed connector. The fa- means 'so/then', signalling sequence or consequence. The -ta ending marks the subject as 'you' (one male), and the attached -hā is the object pronoun 'it/her' (feminine).
5.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, leave behind

6.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

7.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'the day,' very often used to mean 'today' or 'this day.' With the definite article it points to the present day as a defined, known span of time, and by extension can denote 'now' or 'the present moment.'
7.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' is the accusative ending; on a noun of time it commonly marks it as an adverb answering 'when?' — fixing the action to that period ('on the day', 'today').
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

8.meaning: You are forgotten / left aside — to be the one who is neglected and left out of mind, in a present or ongoing/future sense.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The tu- prefix with the internal vowelling marks it as passive addressed to 'you' (the subject undergoes the action rather than doing it). The final -ā is the soft, unchanging ending of a weak-ending verb, here without an additional case/mood vowel.
8.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, leave behind

1.meaning: 'And likewise / and in the same way / and thus' — a connective phrase pointing back to a manner just mentioned and saying 'in that very way…'. Built from 'and' + 'like' + 'that'.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'; the prefix ka- means 'like/as'; 'dhālika' is the demonstrative 'that' (pointing to something distant or already mentioned). Because ka- acts like a preposition, the word after it stands in the genitive, though the demonstrative 'dhālika' keeps a fixed form and shows no visible case change. The whole means 'and just like that / and thus'.

2.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
2.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: He went to excess, was extravagant, overstepped all proper limits — squandering or exceeding the bounds, especially in wrongdoing or wastefulness.

parts.en: he went to excess / was extravagant

4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (Form IV, أَفْعَلَ) pattern, meaning 'he' did the action. The final -a is the past-tense ending for a single male subject ('he …').

5.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
5.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

6.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts and affirms as true — inwardly accepting and giving secure assent, the core act of faith.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV, أَفْعَلَ) pattern. The yu- prefix means 'he'. The vowel-less final -n marks the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles (such as negation or conditions) rather than the plain ongoing form.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, faith, security

7.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
7.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
7.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

8.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

9.meaning: Severe suffering, torment, or punishment inflicted as chastisement. The prefixes add emphasis and definiteness: 'and surely the punishment …'.
9.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case used for a sentence's subject. The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely/indeed', and wa- is 'and'. Together: 'and surely the punishment …'.
9.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, cause pain

10.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
10.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
10.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

11.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
11.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
11.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

12.meaning: And more lasting, more enduring, that which remains longer — the comparative of 'remaining', pointing to what abides and outlasts the rest.
12.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the 'afʿal' pattern ('more/most …') from the root meaning 'to remain'. The final -ā is the fixed soft ending of this weak-rooted form; such comparatives do not change for case.
12.root: ب-ق-ي (b-q-y) — to remain, endure, last, abide

1.meaning: "so have they then not…?" — a clustered opener combining 'so/then' with a questioning 'have they not?'; it poses a rebuking or prompting question about something that has not yet happened, urging reflection.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the questioning a- ('?'), the connective fa- ('so/then'), and lam, which negates and pushes a following present-tense verb into the meaning 'has/did not (do)'. Together they introduce a pointed rhetorical question about a past or completed matter.

2.meaning: He guides, it makes clear, He leads to the right way — to show the path, direct toward what is correct, and lead gently to a goal. 'Hidāya' is guidance both as showing the way and granting success in following it.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The shortened final -i (with no full vowel) is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after a conditional or a negative/command particle and trims the verb's normal ending; the verb's weak final letter drops away here.
2.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly to a goal

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: How many / how much — a particle expressing a large or questioned quantity. It can ask "how many?" or exclaim "how many a…!" to stress abundance.
4.grammar: A quantity word used either to ask about a number ("how many?") or to declare a great number ("how many a…!"). It has no case ending; the noun it counts normally follows it in the singular.

5.meaning: 'We destroyed / We caused to perish' — to bring about ruin, annihilation, or downfall. Combines the verb 'to destroy / cause to perish' with the subject 'we'.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached '-nā' ending is the subject 'we' — it marks the doers of the action as a group including the speaker, with the action completed and in the past.
5.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; (causative) to destroy

6.meaning: Before them — prior to them in time, or ahead of them in sequence; referring to those who came earlier than a given masculine group.
6.grammar: An adverb of time meaning 'before', fixed in the accusative form (the -a ending) as such adverbs typically are. The attached -hum ('them', a masculine plural) is in the genitive as the noun it is linked to, giving 'before them' — earlier than that group.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — precedence, what comes before

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: The generations — successive ages or peoples who lived and passed away one after another; a community of people belonging to a particular era.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the generations'), with the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, marking the word as governed by something before it.
8.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — joining together; an age or generation

9.meaning: "they walk, they go about on foot" — to move along by walking, to make one's way step by step; figuratively, to go about and conduct oneself in the world.
9.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix is the third-person masculine present marker; on its own it is singular ("he/it"), and it is the long -ū vowel together with the -na ending (-ūna) that makes the subject masculine plural, "they (walk)." The final -na is the indicative marker that keeps this plural form in its plain, ongoing present-tense sense.
9.root: م-ش-ي (m-sh-y) — to walk, to go on foot

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: "their dwellings / their dwelling-places" — the plural of a place-noun meaning a residence, home, or place where one settles and finds rest and stillness.
11.grammar: A plural noun of place built on the masākin pattern. The -i ending is genitive, the case taken when a noun is possessed, follows a preposition, or is linked to another noun ("… OF …"); here it precedes the attached pronoun -him, "their" (referring to a masculine plural group).
11.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, settle, be still/at rest

12.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
12.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
