13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
13.root: — (particle)

14.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
14.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

15.meaning: Surely signs, tokens, or clear indications; evidences that point to a greater truth. The prefixed lām adds emphasis ('surely / indeed').
15.grammar: An emphatic particle 'la-' ('surely') joined to an indefinite feminine plural noun ('signs'). The -āt- is the sound feminine plural marker; the final -in (nunation) marks it indefinite. For this plural pattern the -in form serves for both the accusative and the genitive case.

16.meaning: 'for the possessors / owners of' — a phrase meaning those who possess or are endowed with something, governed by 'for' (li-); it is used to attribute a quality to people ('those of …').
16.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') + ulī, the oblique (accusative/genitive) plural of a word meaning 'possessors of, those having.' Ulū/ulī has no singular from its own root and always stands in construct with a following noun ('those endowed WITH …'). The -ī form here is the oblique case required after the preposition.
16.root: — (no triliteral root; a defective noun meaning 'possessor of')

17.meaning: 'Of understanding' / 'of intelligence' — sound reason or intellect; the faculty that restrains a person from folly. The Arabic word literally evokes that which 'holds back' from wrong.
17.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not take a short case-vowel. The word names the reasoning faculty, conceived as that which forbids or restrains a person from error.

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: 'A word / an utterance / a statement' — a single unit of speech; by extension a decree, pronouncement, or settled saying.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation: nominative is the form typically used for the subject of a sentence, and the -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a word'). The feminine -t (tā' marbūṭa) is sounded here because the case ending follows it.
2.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak, word, utterance

3.meaning: 'It preceded / went before / came earlier' — a (feminine) thing that came first or was already established beforehand.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -at ending (here -t with a silent stop) marks the third-person feminine singular ('she/it'), agreeing with a feminine subject, and indicates a completed action ('it has gone before').
3.root: س-ب-ق (s-b-q) — to precede, go ahead, outstrip

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
5.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery, sustaining

6.meaning: 'Surely it would have been / it certainly was' — the verb 'to be' (past tense) carrying an emphatic 'surely', often introducing the result of a hypothetical condition.

parts.en: it was / it would have been

6.grammar: The past-tense verb kāna ('was/were'), third-person masculine singular, with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely'). In conditional sentences this combination commonly heads the consequence clause ('then it surely would have been…'). The verb kāna typically takes a following predicate in the accusative describing the subject's state.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

7.meaning: Something binding and inseparable, an unavoidable consequence that clings fast; an inevitability that necessarily attaches and will not be parted.
7.grammar: A verbal noun conveying clinging necessity. The final -an with tanwīn is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking the word as an object or predicate and signalling that it is indefinite ('a binding necessity').
7.root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m) — to cling, be necessary, be binding/inseparable

8.meaning: And a term, a fixed appointed period or deadline — a span of time set to run until a determined end-point.
8.grammar: A noun preceded by 'and'. The final -un with tanwīn is the indefinite nominative ending, typically marking the word as a subject or as the thing being named/identified, and indefinite ('a term').
8.root: أ-ج-ل (ʾ-j-l) — appointed term, fixed span, deadline

9.meaning: A passive participle meaning 'named, specified, designated, made definite.' It describes something that has been clearly stated and fixed by name — a term that is precisely set rather than vague.
9.grammar: A passive participle (the mu- prefix forms a 'one that is …' word from the Form II intensive pattern, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'named/specified.' It carries the indefinite ending -an, written with alif maqṣūra (a final ya-shaped letter sounded as -ā). Because it ends in this weak final letter, the form stays the same whether nominative, accusative, or genitive — context shows it is describing an indefinite noun.
9.root: س-م-ي (s-m-y) — name, naming; to give or assign a name

1.meaning: A command meaning 'so be patient' or 'so endure steadfastly.' It calls for patient perseverance: bearing hardship, restraining oneself, and holding firm without complaint. The opening 'fa-' connects it to what precedes, giving the sense 'and so…' or 'therefore…'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'be patient!' The vowelless final consonant (sukun on the -r) is the standard ending of a direct order. The prefixed 'fa-' is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'therefore,' linking the command to a preceding statement.

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

5.meaning: And declare Allah's perfection — to glorify, to proclaim Him utterly free of every flaw or imperfection, exalting and praising Him; the command to do so.

parts.en: glorify / declare free of all imperfection

5.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the intensive (Form II, فَعَّلَ) pattern, addressed to one male. The vowel-less final -ḥ is the clipped imperative ending, the bare command form telling 'you' to do the action.
5.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, to declare free of all imperfection

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with the praise of' — joining the preposition 'with/by' to the noun 'praise.' Ḥamd is praise mingled with gratitude and admiration directed to one who deserves it.
6.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' ('with/by') attached to the noun 'praise.' The '-i' ending is genitive, which here follows the preposition and also links 'praise' to a following word ('praise OF …').
6.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise (with gratitude and admiration)

7.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
7.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

8.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
8.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
8.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

9.meaning: The rising, the coming-up (especially of the sun or a star above the horizon) — the act or moment of ascending into view.
9.grammar: A verbal noun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('the rising OF …') or follows a preposition, marking a possessive or 'of' relationship.
9.root: ط-ل-ع (ṭ-l-ʿ) — to rise, come up, ascend (into view)

10.meaning: The sun; the radiant celestial body that gives daylight.
10.grammar: A definite feminine singular noun. The l- prefix means 'the' (its 's' sound assimilates into the following 'sh'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the sun') or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: And before — a connector plus the word marking what comes prior in time or place, the point ahead of something else.
11.grammar: An adverb of time/place meaning 'before'. Its fixed -a ending is the standard form this word takes when it governs a following noun, telling us that something precedes that noun ('before …').
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — before, priority, what comes first

12.meaning: Its setting, its going-down (especially of the sun or a star sinking below the horizon) — the act or moment of disappearing from view.
12.grammar: A verbal noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive (it follows a preposition or links to what precedes), and the attached -hā means 'its/her', so the whole is 'its setting'.
12.root: غ-ر-ب (gh-r-b) — to set, go down, depart westward

13.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
13.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

14.meaning: Hours, watches, periods of the night — the stretches and portions into which the dark hours are divided.
14.grammar: A plural noun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a following noun in an 'of' relationship ('the hours OF …').
14.root: أ-ن-ي (ʾ-n-y) — periods of time, watches, hours

15.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
15.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

16.meaning: So glorify / declare to be utterly free of fault — a command to proclaim that something (the Divine) is far above and beyond every imperfection, exalting and praising it.

parts.en: glorify! / declare free of all fault!

16.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'glorify!' The intensive verb pattern (doubled middle root letter) conveys doing the action thoroughly. The leading fa- means 'so/then', linking the command to what precedes. The bare ending with no added vowel is typical of a direct order.
16.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, extol; to declare free of all imperfection

17.meaning: And the ends, the extremities, the edges and outer limits — the far points or sides of a thing, here a connector plus the plural 'ends'.
17.grammar: A plural noun (plural of 'ṭaraf', an end/extremity). The final -a is the accusative ending, which here marks the word as an object or as an adverb of time/place ('at the ends/edges of …').

18.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
18.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.

19.meaning: So that you may, perhaps you will — a particle of hope or expectation attached to 'you', expressing a desired or anticipated outcome ('in the hope that you …').
19.grammar: A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose ('perhaps / so that'). It governs a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -ka is 'you' (one male) as its subject, giving 'perhaps you / so that you may'.

20.meaning: To be pleased, content, satisfied; to give willing approval and accept gladly.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb from a root whose final letter is weak, so it ends in a long -ā. The ta- prefix marks either a second-person masculine singular ('you') or a third-person feminine singular ('she/it'). It expresses an ongoing or future state of being pleased or content.
20.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, content; goodwill, approval

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: To stretch out, extend, prolong, or reach forth — and by extension to strain or cast one's gaze longingly toward something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a singular 'you' subject. The doubled -nn (the heavy emphatic nūn) attaches to drive the meaning home forcefully, the kind of ending used to strongly affirm or, with a preceding negative/prohibitive, to strongly forbid an act.
2.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — to stretch, extend, prolong

3.meaning: Your two eyes — a dual noun naming the pair of eyes belonging to a single 'you'.
3.grammar: A dual noun (the -ay form signals exactly two) with the attached pronoun -ka 'your' addressing one man. The -ay ending is the dual in its non-nominative (accusative/genitive) shape, the form used when the dual is an object or follows a preposition.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
4.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: We granted enjoyment, provided, or let (someone) have the use and pleasure of something for a time — to furnish with worldly goods and comforts.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb on the doubled (faʿʿala) pattern, which intensifies the sense to actively bestowing enjoyment. The suffix -nā marks a 'we' subject who completed the action.
6.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, provide, give benefit

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'spouses', 'mates', or 'wives' — the plural of a word denoting one of a pair joined together, hence a husband or wife. Context determines whether husbands or wives are meant.
8.grammar: A plural noun with the -an ending, which is accusative and indefinite. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The azC-ā-C shape is a broken-plural pattern. The singular denotes either partner of a married pair.
8.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — to pair, to join as a couple; spouse, mate

9.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
9.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

10.meaning: The bloom, blossom, and bright splendor — the dazzling, flower-like brilliance and showy adornment of something; its fleeting glitter and finery.
10.grammar: A noun meaning a flower's bloom and, by extension, dazzling splendor. It is feminine, so its ta-marbuta is sounded as -t- before the case vowel; the final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the word as an object or as a specifying noun ('the splendor OF …' in object position).
10.root: ز-ه-ر (z-h-r) — to shine, blossom, glow; flower, brightness

11.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
11.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

12.meaning: The nearer life, this present world — the immediate, lower world of here-and-now, contrasted with the lasting life to come; from 'nearer/lower'.
12.grammar: A noun originally a comparative feminine form ('the nearer/lower'), used as a name for the present world. It carries the prefix 'al-' ('the'); its soft final -ā does not change for case, so the word stays the same in all positions.
12.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — to be near/low; nearness, the nearer (life)

13.meaning: So that We may test them — to put people to trial, to examine and prove them, often through hardship or temptation, with the purpose-word 'so that' attached.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of purpose. The prefixed li- means 'so that / in order to'; the na- prefix means 'we'. The -a ending is the subjunctive, the mood a verb takes after a purpose-particle ('so that We may …'). The attached -hum is the object 'them'.
13.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test, try, tempt, put through trial

14.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

15.meaning: And the provision, sustenance, what is granted to support life — that which one is given to live on, here a connector plus 'provision'.
15.grammar: A noun preceded by 'and'. The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being described/identified ('the provision … is …').
15.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, bestow sustenance; provision

16.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
16.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

17.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
17.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
17.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

18.meaning: And more lasting / more enduring / more remaining — comparative: that which abides and persists longer, outlasting what is fleeting.
18.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The word is an elative/comparative adjective ('more lasting' or 'most lasting'), built on the a-…-ā pattern from a root whose last letter is a vowel. Such forms compare or rank, conveying a greater or greatest degree of the quality.

1.meaning: 'And command / and enjoin.' Combines 'and' with the singular imperative 'order' — to instruct or bid someone to do something.
1.grammar: wa- = 'and.' The rest is a singular imperative 'command/order' (you, one person). The form comes from a root whose initial hamza is normally elided, leaving 'mur'; the ending has no vowel (jussive/command form).

2.meaning: Your family, your household and kinfolk — the people belonging to one's home and close circle, with 'your' attached.
2.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the word as an object or as the thing acted upon. The attached -ka means 'your' (one male), giving 'your family'.
2.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, people belonging to something

3.meaning: With/by the ritual prayer — the formal act of worship (ṣalāh) involving prescribed standing, bowing, and prostration. The term denotes devotional prayer as an instituted observance, distinct from informal supplication.
3.grammar: A feminine noun carrying 'the' (al-), governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i is the genitive case, which is exactly what a noun takes after a preposition like bi-; the genitive also typically signals an 'of' relationship to a preceding word.

4.meaning: And be steadfastly patient; a command to endure with constancy and self-restraint, to persevere and hold firm through hardship. The Form VIII pattern intensifies into resolute, sustained patience.
4.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. This is a command (imperative) addressed to one male: 'be patient, persevere!'. It is Form VIII (the infixed -ṭa- after the first root letter, here ص+ت becoming صط), which adds the sense of taking on the action fully — sustained, deliberate patience. The bare ending (sukūn on the last letter) is normal for the singular command.

5.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
5.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'we ask / we request / we question' — to put a request or a question to someone. With an attached object it conveys asking someone (for something).
7.grammar: Present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject 'we'; the bare -u on the stem is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or habitual action ('we ask'). The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male). The middle root letter is a hamza, carried by the seat but not separately sounded here, so the stem reads 'salu'.

8.meaning: 'provision,' 'sustenance,' 'a means of livelihood' — that which is bestowed to sustain and benefit, such as food and resources. 'Rizq' is whatever Allah grants a creature to live on, material or otherwise.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — frequently the role of a stated purpose or explanatory complement ('as provision'), telling for what reason or in what capacity something is given.
8.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide, bestow sustenance

9.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
9.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'we provide / we bestow sustenance upon' — to grant someone provision, livelihood, or the means of life (food, wealth, and every good thing a provider supplies).
10.grammar: Present-tense verb. The na- prefix marks the subject 'we'; the final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or habitual action. The attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male) — the one being provided for.

11.meaning: 'And the final outcome / the end result'; the noun for what comes last — the ultimate consequence or destiny that follows after a course of events.
11.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence. With 'and' it reads 'and the final outcome'.
11.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after; an end/consequence

12.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to / for godliness' — taqwā being the deep, protective God-consciousness that makes one wary of wrongdoing and careful to do right, as if shielding oneself from Allah's displeasure.
12.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ('to', 'for'). It is followed by the noun with its definite article al- ('the'), whose 'l' merges with the noun's initial 't' ('at-taqwā'); the doubling shows in 'li-ttaqwā'. The word ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case.
12.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself; wariness, mindful piety

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
2.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'he comes to / he brings to' — to come or arrive bearing something to someone.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The first root letter is a hamza carried on a connecting alif that is not separately sounded after the prefix, so the stem reads 'tī'. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us' — the ones come to. The action is ongoing or habitual.

4.meaning: With a sign — by means of an indicative token, miracle, or evidentiary proof that points to a truth.
4.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with / by means of' and always pulls the following noun into the genitive. The final -in (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive: 'with a sign', the ending required after this preposition and marking the noun as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
4.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token; a verse of scripture

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'his Lord'. 'Lord' (rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and governs — far richer than a mere title; here joined to 'his'.
6.grammar: The noun 'Lord' with the genitive -i ending followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive case appears because the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… OF his Lord') or follows a preposition. The lengthened -hī reflects how this pronoun is pronounced after an -i vowel.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining and bringing to completion

7.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
7.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'she/it comes to' — to come or arrive at someone. The third-person feminine form is also used when the subject is a grammatically feminine noun (such as a sign or proof 'coming').
8.grammar: Present-tense verb. The ta- prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it') — used for a female or a feminine noun. The first root letter is a hamza on a connecting alif that is not separately sounded after the prefix, so the stem reads 'ti'. The final long ī of the indicative is dropped, leaving a short -i: this shortened (jussive/subjunctive) form is the one taken after particles such as conditions or negation rather than in a plain statement. The attached -him is the object pronoun 'them' (a male or mixed group) — the ones come to.
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

9.meaning: A clear proof, a self-evident sign, a piece of plain and decisive evidence — something so manifest that it removes doubt and establishes the truth of a matter.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('a clear proof [is/does …]').
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, evident, distinct

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: Scriptures, written pages, or revealed sheets — the plural of a 'page/leaf' (ṣaḥīfa), used especially of the sheets of divine revelation.
12.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the scriptures') or follows a preposition. (The 'l' of the article assimilates in sound to the following ṣ, hence 'aṣ-ṣuḥuf'.)

13.meaning: The first, the foremost, the initial one — the feminine form of the ordinal 'first', denoting that which comes before all others in order or time.
13.grammar: A definite ordinal adjective (with al-, 'the'), the feminine of 'first', so it describes a feminine noun. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case; it conveys priority in sequence ('the first/former').
13.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede, origin

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: That We … — an emphatic linking particle 'that' fused with the pronoun 'We.' 'Anna' introduces and asserts a fact ('that indeed …'), and the attached 'We' names the doer (a majestic or plural 'We').
2.grammar: An emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā 'we.' This family of particles takes a following noun/pronoun in the accusative as its subject, so -nā here functions as that subject: 'that We …'. It firmly introduces a stated fact.

3.meaning: We destroyed them; a verb for bringing ruin and annihilation upon a group, with those people as the object destroyed.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb in the causative pattern (Form IV, 'to cause to perish'). The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking a completed action by a first-person plural doer. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (those destroyed).
3.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; (Form IV) to destroy, ruin

4.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
4.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
6.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'they would certainly say,' carrying an emphatic stress: it expresses what a group of people would inevitably utter or assert. The opening particle adds the force of a sworn or guaranteed outcome.
7.grammar: The la- prefix is an emphatic particle meaning 'surely/certainly,' often answering an implied condition ('they would surely…'). The verb is past-tense in form; the -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The silent alif after the wāw is a spelling convention with no sound.

8.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

8.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

9.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
9.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'you sent / you dispatched' — to send forth a person (such as a messenger) or to release/let loose something. Addressed to a single male.
10.grammar: Past-tense verb of the 'afʿala' pattern (which adds a causative 'to make/send'). The suffix -ta marks the doer as 'you' (one male) and the action as completed in the past.

11.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
11.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
11.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

12.meaning: "a messenger / an envoy" — one who is sent bearing a message; 'rasūl' is an emissary commissioned to convey something on behalf of the one who sent him, especially a prophet sent with a divine message.
12.grammar: A masculine noun on the faʿūl pattern, indefinite ('a messenger'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥ) is the indefinite accusative case, the form used for the direct object of a verb; the written alif carries this ending.
12.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, messenger

13.meaning: 'so that we might follow' — the verb 'we follow / we pursue / we adhere to' (going after someone or something, taking it as a guide or example), introduced by 'so that, in order that'.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb of the 'iftaʿala' pattern (here meaning to follow closely). The na- prefix marks the subject 'we'. The final vowel is -a (subjunctive mood), the form taken in a purpose or result clause; here the connective fa- ('so that') introduces that clause — 'so that we may follow'.
13.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

14.meaning: "Your signs / Your verses" — 'āyāt' are signs, tokens, or proofs that point to something beyond themselves; the word also denotes the verses of revelation. With 'Your' it means signs/verses belonging to a single addressee.
14.grammar: A feminine plural noun (singular āya) with the possessive pronoun '-ka' ('your') attached. The 'i' ending on the noun is the genitive case, used here because the noun is possessed (linked to the following 'your'); the sound feminine plural takes this same '-i' for both object and genitive roles.
14.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, token

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
16.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
16.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'we are abased / we are humiliated / we become lowly' — to be brought low, disgraced, or made contemptible.
18.grammar: Present-tense verb with the na- prefix marking the subject 'we'. This is a geminate (doubled-consonant) root, so its two identical last letters merge into one doubled ل. The final -a is the subjunctive mood: the indicative ending -u is simply dropped and -a appears on the doubled lam. The subjunctive is the form used after particles of purpose, condition, or negation rather than in a plain statement.
18.root: ذ-ل-ل (dh-l-l) — to be low, humble, abased

19.meaning: 'and we are disgraced' — the verb 'we are put to shame / we are humbled and brought to ruin', joined by 'and'.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb with na- ('we'). The verb ends in a long ā written as a 'broken' alif (alif maqṣūra) because its final root letter is weak; in this form the mood vowel is not separately pronounced. The wa- prefix simply links it to what precedes ('and …').
19.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, shamed, humiliated

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'all,' 'each,' 'every,' or 'the whole.' It denotes totality — that the entirety of a group or thing is included.
2.grammar: A noun in the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (the -un ending), which marks it as indefinite and as the subject or doer of a sentence. Standing alone with tanwīn it carries the sense 'everyone / all of them' as an independent subject.
2.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

3.meaning: One who waits, watches, and lies in expectation — someone awaiting an outcome, biding time to see what will befall (often with the nuance of watching for another's fate).
3.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) of the 'tafaʿʿala' pattern, naming the one performing the action — 'a waiter / one who lies in wait'. The mu- prefix forms the doer-noun. The ending -un is the nominative case with nunation (the -n marking it as indefinite, 'a …'), the form used for a subject or predicate.
3.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch, lie in expectation

4.meaning: Then wait / then await / then watch and bide your time — a command to expect an outcome, holding back to see what comes. Tarabbaṣa is to wait expectantly, sometimes warily, for something to unfold.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb (Form V) addressed to a group of males or a mixed group, prefixed by fa- ('then/so'), which links it to what precedes as a consequence. The plural-command ending -ū means 'you all, do this!' — so it directs a group to wait. (The written alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.)
4.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, lie in wait, watch for an outcome

5.meaning: 'Then you will soon come to know.' A verb of knowing addressed to a group, prefaced by 'then' and the near-future marker 'will soon', typically used as a warning that the truth of a matter will become plain.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb meaning 'you (plural) know'. The 'ta-…-ūna' frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The prefix 'sa-' places it in the near future ('will soon'), and 'fa-' links it to what precedes ('then / so'). The retained final 'na' (in '-ūna') shows the indicative, a plain statement of fact. Often delivered as a threat or solemn warning.
5.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, to know

6.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
6.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
6.root: — (pronoun)

7.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
7.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

8.meaning: The path, the road, the way — especially a clear, broad highway; used figuratively for the way of life or course one travels.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the path') or follows a preposition. (The 'l' of the article assimilates in sound to the following ṣ, hence 'aṣ-ṣirāṭ'.)
8.root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ) — path, road, way

9.meaning: Even, straight, level, sound and well-balanced — describing a way that is smooth and correctly aligned, free of crookedness or fault.
9.grammar: An adjective with the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun. (The 'l' of the article assimilates in sound to the following s, hence 'as-sawiyy'.)
9.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, balanced, sound

10.meaning: And whoever / and the one who: 'and' joined to a word meaning 'who(ever)' — referring to a person or persons, often introducing a condition ('whoever does…') or a relative clause ('the one who…').
10.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the pronoun 'man' ('who / whoever'), which refers to people. 'man' itself does not change for case; the final -i is only a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting before the next word.

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'he became guided / he found and followed the right way' — to accept guidance and walk the correct path, to be rightly directed.
11.grammar: Past-tense verb of the 'iftaʿala' pattern (here reflexive: to take guidance for oneself). It is third-person masculine singular ('he'). The verb ends in a long ā written as a 'broken' alif (alif maqṣūra) because its final root letter is weak. The opening 'i' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.
11.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way
